findings.title: Advanced negative-offset branch raises ValueError from Django slicing
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The inline comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is incorrect. The advanced feature therefore always fails with a 500 for any negative cursor offset, and the 'access beyond normal bounds' behaviour it advertises is never reachable.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime sort keys
findings.body: The endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. get_item_key calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`, which is a datetime object, so this raises TypeError on the first result. Unlike DateTimePaginator, there is no conversion to a numeric timestamp. Likewise value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value rather than a datetime, so build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer. Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` by a superuser or global-access member, with at least one audit log row, will fail.

findings.title: Negative offset on prev cursors still reaches Django slicing and crashes
findings.body: The new start_offset logic clamps negative offsets only when `not cursor.is_prev`. For prev cursors, start_offset = offset, which can be negative. Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers for the offset field (int(bits[1])), so a client-supplied prev cursor such as `123:-5:1` reaches `queryset[-5:stop]` and raises ValueError, producing a 500. This affects every BasePaginator subclass, including DateTimePaginator used by all audit log requests.

findings.title: Silent behaviour change for all paginators when next-cursor offset is negative
findings.body: The clamp `max(0, offset)` is applied globally in BasePaginator.get_result, not only on the new optimized path. Previously a negative offset on a next cursor raised an error. Now it silently returns the page from the start, for every endpoint using DateTimePaginator or other BasePaginator subclasses. This changes API behaviour for all callers without a gating flag, and the comment describing it as a performance optimization does not justify it.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported, but nothing enforces or supports them
findings.body: The added comment says the Cursor enables 'efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions', but Cursor.__init__ merely calls int(offset), and the downstream slicing code in paginator.py cannot handle negative starts. The comment misdescribes the behaviour and will mislead future maintainers.

findings.title: Unreleased experimental pagination switch gated by a query parameter on a public endpoint
findings.body: The endpoint now switches paginator implementation based on a user-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter, gated only by is_superuser or has_global_access. This adds an undocumented, untested code path to a public (EXPERIMENTAL) API. The optimized path is broken (see paginator.py get_item_key), so any admin who sets this parameter gets a 500. The change also adds no tests and the PR description ('Test 1') does not explain the intent or the behaviour change.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result nearly verbatim
findings.body: The new class copies most of BasePaginator.get_result, including the prev-cursor filtering and build_cursor call, and adds only a branch that is itself broken. Any future fix to the base logic would have to be duplicated here, increasing the chance of divergence. Overriding only the specific behaviour would be safer.

findings.title: No tests added for the new paginator behaviour or the endpoint switch
findings.body: The PR changes pagination behaviour (negative offset handling, a new paginator class, and a new endpoint branch), but adds no tests. Given that the new code paths raise exceptions for datetime keys and negative offsets, tests exercising optimized_pagination=true and negative cursors would have caught these failures.
